title: Twitter r10 pro опыт эксплуатации и апгрейд.

takeaways.text: After about 1,500 km the main failure was an electronic shift lever that stopped working, apparently after water got in during washing; he advises sealing the gaps.
The seller sent a replacement lever for the cost of shipping only, about 2,500 rubles against roughly 10,000 for the part.
The wheels needed truing after the season and the rear hub bearings began to creak and drag; otherwise nothing creaked or came loose.
The stock alloy bar is very heavy (he estimates about 700 g); a carbon bar saved about half a kilogram, and he also recommends better tires.
He notes the bike was then available for about 85,000 rubles with electronic shifting and carbon wheels.

disclosure: Owner video; no sponsorship is stated. The bike is an R10 Pro with electronic shifting and carbon wheels; its generation is not stated.
summary: A Russian owner's report on a TWITTER R10 Pro after a season of about 1,500 km, with faults and upgrades; Russian automatic captions.
